chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthayfir, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"When you arrive in Mecca - on the Day of Tarwiyah and the sun has set - and you do not have a Tamattu' [Hajj], proceed with your Hajj as it is [as Qiran or Ifrad]."

The correct interpretation of these narrations is what we mentioned: that whoever fears missing the two standings [of Arafat and Muzdalifah] if he engages in Ihlal [staying in the state of Ihram without exiting to Tamattu'], he should proceed in his Ihram and make it a singular Hajj (Hajj al-Mufrad).

And whoever does not fear missing that, or is confident that he will reach both standings, then he should exit Ihram [for Umrah] and then enter Ihram for Hajj, according to what we have previously established.
And that which indicates this meaning is what he narrated:

key_terms.الْإِحْلَال: Ihlal (remaining in the state of Ihram without exiting for Umrah)
key_terms.الْمَوْقِفَيْنِ: The two standings (of Arafat and Muzdalifah)
key_terms.مُتْعَةٌ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj with a break in between)

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if they arrive in Mecca late on the Day of Tarwiyah?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the practical application of Hajj types based on time availability, a key concern for pilgrims arriving in Mecca on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah. It establishes that fear of missing the Standing at Arafat (*fawt al-mawqif*) justifies remaining in a singular Ihram (*Hajj Munfarid*), while confidence in timely completion permits the preferred *Hajj Tamattu'* (Umrah then Hajj). This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on ensuring the validity of the core pillar of Arafat over ritual preference.
